title: Cost optimization: defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-economics tooling
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduce conservative default batching and caching config, add quantization profiles for common model families, and ship a unit-economics report generator + CLI command for teams to estimate tps/cost tradeoffs.
description: Motivation: Customers running diverse workloads often leave batching, KV-cache, and quantization settings at defaults that are suboptimal for unit economics. This PR implements conservative defaults and a lightweight automation flow that recommends per-route batching/caching parameters, adds curated quantization profiles for Llama and Mistral families, and provides a unit-economics tool to surface expected cost/latency impacts. Changes are gated behind feature flags and rolled out to a small percentage of traffic for 48h before full rollout. Summary of changes: - Add new config keys and defaults: routing.batch_size_hint, routing.max_concurrency_hint, caching.prefix_cache_enabled (default true for text-gen), caching.kv_ttl_seconds (default 600) - Implement heuristics that compute adaptive batch windows based on request size and historical p99 latency - Add quant_profiles/{llama,mistral}.yaml with recommended q4_0/q8_0 profiles and expected accuracy delta annotations - Add unit-economics CLI command (`redwood tools unit-econ --route <route> --model <model>`) that pulls recent traffic histograms and simulates per-token cost under candidate configs - Telemetry: new metrics unit_econ.estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens, routing.batch_window_ms, routing.effective_batch_size - Console: UI exposes recommended config and a "simulate" button (UI change minimal; mostly backend-ready) Rollout plan: - Feature flag alpha.enable_optimize_defaults initially off in config-service - Deploy runtime and tooling to staging and run canary with internal traffic - Enable 2% of production traffic for 48h, compare unit-econ metrics and p99 latency; if regressions <= 5% in latency and >=10% cost reduction, increase to 25% - Full rollout after sign-off by SRE and Product Performance. Testing: - Unit tests for batching heuristic and cache TTL calculations - Integration tests for quant profile selection and model compatibility checks - E2E smoke: validate CLI output on sample traffic dumps - Load test: synthetic traffic with mixed short/long sequences shows ~12-18% cost reduction on CPU-backed models and 6-10% on GPU heavy tails Compatibility notes: quant profiles are opt-in per-deployment and require runtime to support quantized kernels; fallback to FP32 if unsupported. Backwards compatibility maintained by defaulting to previous behavior when feature flag is off. Migration notes: ops may set route-level overrides to opt out for latency-sensitive routes. Related: ENG-4123 (optimizer backlog), PM-298 (pricing initiative).
commit_summary: 3 commits: 1) infra: add feature flags and new config schema; 2) runtime: batching/caching heuristics and metrics; 3) tools: quant profiles and unit-econ CLI + docs
review_comments: Evan Miller: Can you add a short circuit for tiny requests so we don't add batching overhead to sub-32 token calls?
Priya Shah (author): Added a fast-path in batching.go to bypass windowing for requests shorter than 32 tokens; updated unit tests.
Carlos Gomez: Please ensure quant profiles include expected accuracy delta and a link to evaluation harness results.
Priya Shah (author): Included accuracy_delta field in profiles and linked to eval run 2026-02-20 in the YAML comments.
Lina Chen: Suggest adding a CLI flag to output a per-route granular CSV for finance review.
Priya Shah (author): Added --export-csv flag and a minimal formatter; docs updated.
Evan Miller: CI flaky test 'batching_window_test' failed once; reran and passed. Approving.
Carlos Gomez: LGTM after minor nits fixed. Approving.
notes_on_metrics: Staging canary: estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens down 14% on avg for mixed traffic; p99 latency +2.8% on small routes, <1% on tail-heavy routes. Production 2% rollout validated with no alerts.
merge_commit_message:
squash: cost(opt): defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling

Conservative defaults, adaptive batching heuristics, curated quant profiles for Llama/Mistral, and a unit-economics CLI to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs. Feature gated behind alpha.enable_optimize_defaults.

Closes ENG-4123, PM-298
post_merge_tasks: Add config knobs to Dedicated deploy docs
incident_bubble_up: No incident triggered. Load tests revealed a flaky test that CI reran; no customer impact.
author_pr_comments: Thanks for reviews — I've left the feature flag off by default. We'll follow the rollout plan and notify SRE before bumping traffic percentage.
Followups: telemetry dashboard card and an ops runbook for rolling back route overrides.
ui_changes: Small: expose recommended config and a simulate button; backend-backed, frontend PR will follow in a separate repo.
security_considerations: No sensitive data changes. Unit-econ tool reads aggregated histograms only; all exports respect team RBAC and KMS for any persisted artifacts.
qa_notes: Run tools/unit_econ against sample_traffic.json and verify output CSV matches golden sample located at tests/golden/unit_econ.csv. Ensure quant profile selection falls back on unsupported kernels.
changelog_snippet: Defaults for smarter batching/caching and quantization recommendations to reduce per-token costs; new unit-economics tooling to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs.
public_admin_note: Enterprise customers can opt in to the quant profiles via support ticket until the UI is available.
backport: No backport planned; changes are feature-flag gated and non-breaking. If needed, backport to release/2026-02 in small patch.
estimated_savings: 12-15% median cost reduction in tested mixed workloads; numbers vary by model family and deployment type.
